name: Logging Strategy Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday logging strategy work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical logging strategy tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday logging strategy work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical logging strategy tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep logging strategy changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Prefer the simplest logging strategy approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Before starting logging strategy work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. When logging strategy guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Validate logging strategy outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to logging strategy (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep logging strategy outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. When multiple logging strategy strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen logging strategy approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Document any non-obvious logging strategy decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated logging strategy concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new logging strategy abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop logging strategy edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of logging strategy correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these logging strategy guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
